pillars.name: Built for the middle
pillars.definition: The 4,000+ community hospital foundations raising $2M–$15M a year that healthcare philanthropy was never designed for: too big for templates, too small for enterprise retainers, expected to perform like the top 50 systems on a fraction of the staff and data.
in_scope: why sector benchmarks and models don't fit mid-size shops
what strategy built for this scale looks like
out_of_scope: academic medical center and nine-figure campaign playbooks
pillars.why_now: The single most ownable position in this entire pilot. It names an audience by size, that audience recognizes itself instantly, and no incumbent is claiming it — AHP's own benchmarking segments community hospitals but the strategy content is still built around high performers and large systems.

proof_assets.name: Months of 1:1 conversations with hospital CDOs
proof_assets.notes: Her renewable supply — protect the interview cadence

pillars.name: Two clocks: the quarter and the decade
pillars.definition: The structural mismatch between how boards ask for fundraising results and how relationships actually mature — and what it does to CDO tenure when a relationship business is reported on a sales calendar.
in_scope: what CDOs wish their boards understood
pillars.why_now: It is the pain her buyer feels every quarter, it comes straight from her own interview question, and the ~18-month development-director tenure figure gives it a number.

proof_assets.name: 'What's the one thing you wish your board understood?' — months of CDO answers
proof_assets.notes: Strongest asset she has; keep asking it

incumbent.strength: Speaks to boards, not to CDOs
incumbent.how_we_differ: She speaks for the CDO to the board — the same content, aimed the other direction.

pillars.name: Know them or reach them
pillars.definition: The choice between a volume-led foundation that measures reach and a relevance-led one that measures resonance, made concrete: the four rooms of a donor file, and what donor-base concentration means when the top of the file ages out.
in_scope: donor file depth and relationship tiers
volume vs relevance as a strategic choice
pillars.why_now: It gives her flagship audience something to DO, and it pairs the industry's giving-is-up story with the fragility underneath it.

proof_assets.name: The four rooms: sidewalk, front porch, living room, kitchen table
proof_assets.notes: Memorable and hers to own; Todd Hiestand quote from Converge

proof_assets.notes: Every queued post across all three seats is Converge-derived. Rich, but a finite well — see notes.

incumbent.how_we_differ: The four-rooms metaphor is a strategy frame a CDO can use in a board meeting; software content can't do that.

pillars.name: Saying it out loud
pillars.definition: What hospital development leaders say quietly and won't say on a stage — the rehearsed calm before a board meeting, the campaign that isn't fine — and treating that candor as part of the job rather than a lapse in it.
in_scope: leadership anxiety specific to healthcare development leaders
naming pressure as a leadership practice
what CDOs carry that their teams already sense
out_of_scope: nonprofit CEO burnout at sector level — that is Trent's; keep this to the CDO seat
